newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico soybean meal prices down on oversupply -ASA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico soybean meal prices down on oversupply -ASA.

text.p: Prices for soybean meal in Mexican have slumped since early May on reports of industry oversupplies, local offices of the United Soybean Board (USB) and the American Soybean Association (ASA) said Wednesday.
In an update, USB/ASA said meal prices were down at 2,800 pesos per tonne (around $354) from 2,900 to 2,950 pesos seen in early May.
It gave no FOB destinations for the prices.

Crushers Hidrogenadora in Mexicali close to the U.S. border are still crushing, despite their competitors' beliefs that they should be importing crude, and they are selling in central states, including Jalisco state, the USB/ASA said.

Guadalajara crushers (also in Jalisco state) have had to drop prices in the face of the strong competition on meal, it added. Other major crushers are also reportedly at near capacity and supplying to center states.

"Gamesa is crushing in Cd Obregon and is sending its meal to the southern part of the country as well as the center, Jalisco again. Also, The new Cargill plant in Tula is crushing near capacity and is offering meal at discounts. So meal is at lower prices than should be the case given current bean prices," USB/ASA added.

Cargill de Mexico, Cargill Inc.'s local subsidiary, opened a soybean crushing plant at Tula in the state of Hidalgo in early February. It is designed to process 1,500 tonnes of soybeans per day, producing meal and oil for the Mexican market.
